connect.accepts: An ADO.NET connection string, an mssql:// or JDBC URL, or host,port/database. Azure SQL without a user name signs in with your az login (Entra ID).
A postgres:// or JDBC URL, libpq's key=value pairs, an Npgsql connection string, or host:port/database.

last_actual_plan.message: PostgreSQL doesn't keep the actual plan of past runs
last_actual_plan.hint: auto_explain can write them to the server log, which Culprit can't read over SQL. Open the query in the editor with real values and use Analyze: it runs inside a transaction that is rolled back.

operator_progress.message: PostgreSQL reports a running statement's progress, not each step's
operator_progress.hint: Its plan doesn't change while it runs: ask for the plan once.

connect.accepts: A mysql://, mariadb:// or JDBC URL, a .NET connection string (Server=…;Uid=…), or host:port/database.

last_actual_plan.message: MySQL and MariaDB don't keep the actual plan of past runs
last_actual_plan.hint: Measure it instead: Analyze runs the statement's recorded text once inside a read-only transaction.

operator_progress.message: MySQL reports a running statement's progress, not each step's
operator_progress.hint: Its plan doesn't change while it runs: ask for the plan once.

connect.accepts: The database file. Culprit opens it read-only and needs nothing from your app.

deadlocks.message: SQLite records no deadlocks: one writer at a time holds the file
deadlocks.hint: A transaction that can't get the write lock waits busy_timeout, then gets SQLITE_BUSY in the application: its logs say when.

last_actual_plan.message: SQLite's plans have no actual rows or timings: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows the access path only
last_actual_plan.hint: Use the estimated plan; time the statement in the application to see how long it takes.

measures_runs.message: SQLite's plans have no actual rows or timings: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows the access path only
measures_runs.hint: Use the estimated plan; time the statement in the application to see how long it takes.

operator_progress.message: SQLite has no server, so no sessions to show
operator_progress.hint: A writer that has to wait gets SQLITE_BUSY in the application: its logs say when.

periods.message: SQLite keeps no statement history to compare two periods of
periods.hint: Add the log your framework writes to the connection, scan before and after the change, and compare the two reports' queries.

plan_estimates.message: SQLite's plans have no actual rows or timings: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows the access path only
plan_estimates.hint: Use the estimated plan; time the statement in the application to see how long it takes.

sessions.message: SQLite has no server, so no sessions to show
sessions.hint: A writer that has to wait gets SQLITE_BUSY in the application: its logs say when.

sign_in.message: A SQLite file takes no sign-in: Culprit opens it read-only from disk

wait_sample.message: SQLite has no server, so nothing records what it waits on
wait_sample.hint: Time spent waiting for the write lock shows up in the application as SQLITE_BUSY or slow commits.

writes.message: Culprit opens SQLite files read-only, so it never changes one
writes.hint: Run it with the sqlite3 shell or from the application, then scan again to see the effect.
